messages:
rachel: New-hire flagged a weird onboarding hiccup in the sample: when the client reconnects during an auth refresh we sometimes see a fragment re-order or duplicated tail. Reproable reliably on my machine.

diego: Nice. Which SDK/version?

rachel: Node SDK v1.0.0-beta in the quickstart sample. Steps: 1) start sample stream, 2) send a prompt, 3) trigger ctrl-c mid-stream, 4) restart within ~120ms. Failure modes: duplicate final tokens, or small fragment appearing before the resume token.

mina: That sounds similar to an auth-refresh + retry path race. Our retry path replays buffered writes; if resume metadata is also applied clients can see duplicates.

rachel: Minimal curl repro for infra folk:
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{"prompt":"onboard race"}'
# kill + restart client quickly to simulate immediate reconnect
```

ops-bot: Observed 14 onboarding failures in last 48h for /v1/stream in eu-central attributable to short reconnect windows. Suggest default reconnect jitter for samples.

diego: Two practical fixes: server-side monotonic per-chunk seq in resume metadata; SDK: emit explicit "resume" event with last-seen-seq and dedupe on client. Also, make teardown skip debounce so buffered chunks are flushed deterministically on abort.

mina: I can add a small change in the Node SDK to expose a "resumed" event and a small helper that drops repeated seq ids. Also add unit tests simulating auth-rotation + ctrl-c.

rachel: Can we also add a quickstart note: "If you see duplicated tokens on reconnect, add 200ms backoff or upgrade sample token TTL"? New devs keep hitting this during tutorials.

ci-bot: linked CI: https://ci.redwood.ai/build/9012 (streaming-onboard-flaky)

mina: I'll add a reproducible e2e in the streaming harness covering: proxy coalesce + auth rotate + ctrl-c immediate reconnect. Parity matrix: node/python/rust.

diego: One more thought: lightweight server header 'x-rw-seq' with seq ids would make client reordering/dedupe trivial and backward-compatible. Ops: any perf implications?

ops-bot: No significant perf hit. We can add header with small int per chunk; rollout via server tag. Recommend testing with proxy buffering on/off.

rachel: Filed RED-5012 and added to onboarding checklist with temp workaround and test flag.  https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-5012

diego: Great. Prioritize SDK event + small server seq header + parity tests. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:
